reports.title: Symbotic Reports Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026 Results

guidance.heading: OUTLOOK
section: For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Symbotic expects revenue of $805 million to $825 million and adjusted EBITDA2 of $110 million to $120 million.

desk.headline: Revenue up 26% to $778m, slightly above estimates; adjusted EPS $0.17 beat; Q1 outlook of $805–825m revenue

other.label: Net income (GAAP)
other.change: vs a $9.0m loss a year ago

results: Revenue rose 26% to $778m, just above the $774m estimate; Systems revenue grew 24% to $722m.
Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $114m and GAAP net income was $55m, against a loss a year ago.
For the full year, revenue rose 25% to $2.80bn and Symbotic posted its first full year of GAAP profit ($133m).
Free cash flow was $353m in the quarter and $596m for the year; cash reached $2.0bn.
84 systems were in deployment and 59 were operational at year end; backlog stood at $22.3bn.

guidance.summary: For Q1 fiscal 2027 Symbotic expects revenue of $805–825m and adjusted EBITDA of $110–120m. It does not give a full-year forecast, but said fiscal 2027 revenue will lean more to the second half.

points: CEO Rick Cohen said the expanded Walmart agreement should add nearly $7bn to backlog in Q1 fiscal 2027, with most of the financial benefit in later years.
Symbotic is installing its in-store SymMicro system at two Walmart stores, the first due live in January; Cohen pointed to a possible 400-store order worth over $5bn.
CFO Izzy Martins expects adjusted gross margins to stay broadly stable in the first half, with operating costs rising on acquisitions and R&D.
About 16% of the backlog is expected to turn into revenue over the next 12 months; the next-generation storage structure should pick up in the second half.
Management said acquisitions come ahead of share buybacks in its use of cash.
